logline.title: The Last Tram
logline.theme: A night-shift tram conductor receives a letter from a passenger who never came back; when he appears at the last stop, she must decide whether to open the door.
logline.summary: Mei, a Hong Kong tram conductor, finds an envelope on the last tram of the night. The man who left it is waiting at the final stop, soaked by rain, and the film ends on the decision she does not make aloud.

scripts.script_text:
THE LAST TRAM

FADE IN:

EXT. HONG KONG TRAM DEPOT - NIGHT

Rain needles the corrugated roof. A single green tram waits under a sodium lamp. MEI (30s), a conductor in a faded uniform, wipes fog from its windows with her sleeve.

INT. TRAM - NIGHT

Mei walks the empty aisle, punching holes in the air. At the back row, a dry envelope lies on the seat.

Inside is a photograph of a man on a ferry, his back to the camera. On the reverse, one line: "Last tram. 11:40. If you still remember."

EXT. TRAM STOP - NIGHT

Mei stands at the open door. The city blinks past in wet neon. A MAN (40s), soaked through, runs toward the tram.

Their eyes meet through the glass.

MEI
You're late.

MAN
I know.

She does not open the door.

MEI
So am I.

FADE OUT.

logline.title: The Blue Hour
logline.theme: An ageing Sham Shui Po tailor prepares a suit for his daughter, who is leaving Hong Kong; the fitting becomes the last honest conversation they will have.
logline.summary: Kam, a tailor in Sham Shui Po, fits a suit for a daughter who has already decided to leave. Through measurements, an old photograph and a final mirror check, they say what they have avoided for years.

scripts.script_text:
THE BLUE HOUR

FADE IN:

INT. TAILOR SHOP - SHAM SHUI PO - DUSK

Blue evening light falls through the shop window. KAM (60s) works at a sewing machine, surrounded by bolts of cloth and a radio playing an old Cantonese song.

The bell above the door rings. A WOMAN (30s), his daughter, enters carrying a suit bag.

KAM
You came back.

WOMAN
I needed a fitting.

He does not look up.

KAM
Stand still.

He measures her shoulders. The tape is cold. Neither speaks.

WOMAN
I'm leaving on Friday.

KAM
I know.

He cuts a loose thread.

KAM
Lift your arms.

She does. In the mirror, their eyes meet.

WOMAN
Will you come to the airport?

KAM
The shop doesn't close for anyone.

She lowers her arms. The radio song ends.

WOMAN
Then don't come.

He holds out his hand for the tape. She gives it to him.

FADE OUT.

logline.title: The Last Booth
logline.theme: A late-night radio host takes one last call from a listener who has been trying to reach him for years; the city becomes the only witness to their conversation.
logline.summary: Lok, a Hong Kong late-night radio host, is about to leave the city. A caller he has never met tells him a story that makes the studio feel smaller and the city outside suddenly personal.

scripts.script_text:
THE LAST BOOTH

FADE IN:

INT. RADIO STATION - NIGHT

A narrow studio. LOK (30s) sits behind the microphone, headphones around his neck. The ON AIR sign glows red.

LOK
Last call before we close.

The phone line blinks. He presses it.

CALLER (V.O.)
I've called you every night for three years.

Lok looks at the timer. 3:12 AM.

LOK
Why tonight?

CALLER (V.O.)
Because I'm leaving Hong Kong tomorrow.

Outside the window, neon reflects on wet concrete. Lok leans toward the mic.

LOK
Where are you going?

CALLER (V.O.)
Somewhere without a harbour.

Lok smiles, then stops.

LOK
What do you want me to say?

CALLER (V.O.)
That you remember me.

Lok looks at the empty chair opposite him.

LOK
I don't.

CALLER (V.O.)
Liar.

She hangs up. The studio falls silent. The ON AIR sign blinks out.

FADE OUT.
